comment_regular: Release only a BSTPersistentList's already-free node chain at +0x0C to the global NiTList node pool, then clear that free-chain pointer and terminate the active tail link. It never destroys active or free-node RenderPass payload pointers.

Verified cleanup 2026-09-30: pop each old local free node in forward-chain order; under native CS B33F00 set node+4=0, node.next=current global free head B33EAC, then global free head=node. This reverses the returned chain; node+8 payload remains untouched. Afterwards local freeHead=0 and active tail.next=0. Bucket7AC9A0 subsequently transfers active head into freeHead and clears active head/tail/count unless frozen. Fallout8220EF38 is the homologous CleanUnusedNodes; its spin-lock nesting differs from this per-node critical-section sequence.
DX11 replacement authority audit 2026-10-01: cleanup of a nonempty local free chain writes the shared native pool head at B33EAC under the real CRITICAL_SECTION B33F00 (base B33E90+70), with native owner thread at B33F78 and nesting at B33F7C. A captured BuildCommit result that returns old free nodes therefore requires pool ownership again at application and throughout rollback; checking only the planning boolean is insufficient. A bucket with no old free chain avoids this shared-pool write, but still requires separate lifetime and local list-writer proof. Renderer+80 lock alone does not replace this pool lock.
Verified comparative family 2026-10-01: Fallout PPC 8220EF38 BSTPersistentList<NiTPointerAllocator<unsigned int>,NiGeometry*>::CleanUnusedNodes has the same free-chain walk, shared-pool return, list+C clear and active-tail termination as this Oblivion implementation. Its recursive BSSpinLock plus outer whole-chain lock differs from Oblivion Win32 per-node CRITICAL_SECTION use. Related append family: Oblivion 7ABDE0 and Fallout 82210150 reuse list free nodes or acquire from the allocator, append the existing payload pointer without refcount transfer, and update tail/count. This correlation does not prove scene-resource lifetime or all writer exclusion.
